pages.name: Still there?
pages.task: Air shut in a cylinder fills 300 cm³ at 6 bar absolute. A heavier load raises its pressure to 9 bar absolute, at the same temperature. What volume does the air fill now?
pages.why: Pressure times volume stays at 6 × 300, which makes 1800. So the volume is 1800 ÷ 9, which is 200 cm³. The heavier load pushes the rod in.

pages.task: The motor runs and no solenoid is energised. What does the ram do?
pages.answer: It holds, and the pump's oil goes back to the tank
pages.why: The sheet draws the valve at rest, with its middle box against the ports. That box joins P to T and blocks A and B. So the pump's oil goes back to the tank at low pressure, and the ram holds.

pages.name: The other side
pages.task: Which parts does the rod side's oil pass on its way to the tank, in order?
pages.why: The check valve is shut this way, so the rod side's oil leaves through the flow control. The left box joins B to T, so the oil runs back to the tank. Without that path the ram could barely move.

pages.name: On the work
pages.text: The flow control lets the rod side's oil out slowly, so it sets the ram's speed. This pump pushes out the same amount every turn. The slowed cylinder takes less, so the pressure rises until the relief valve opens. The spare oil goes over it. So the relief valve's setting decides how hard the ram presses. Here the ram has stopped on the work. All the pump's oil now runs over the relief valve to the tank, and the needle sits on the relief mark.

pages.name: What sets the squeeze?
pages.task: The ram is pressing the work and -Y1 is still on. Which part decides how hard it presses?
pages.why: The ram cannot move, so the pressure rises until the relief valve opens. Its setting is the highest the pressure can reach. So it decides how hard the ram presses.

pages.name: Back up
pages.text: Energise -Y2 and the crossed box joins P to B and A to T. Oil reaches the rod side through the check valve. The piston side drains to the tank, and the ram goes back up. Here both solenoids are off, and the ram holds part way up. Before that, -Y2 was on. Oil ran from P to B through the check valve into the rod side, and from A to T to the tank. Then -Y2 went off, and the middle box blocked A and B.

pages.name: Into the rod side
pages.task: -Y2 is on. Which way does most of the oil reach the rod side?
pages.why: Going into the rod side, the oil lifts the check valve's ball off its seat. So most of it passes the flow control by. The ram goes up quickly, and comes down at the flow control's speed.

pages.name: The same job in air
pages.text: The same job in air uses a 5/2 valve. Energise -Y3 and the supply fills the piston side. The rod side's air leaves through an exhaust port, into the room. Air also squeezes. So a cylinder holding a load on shut-in air gives as the load grows. Here -Y3 is on. The supply runs into the piston side, the rod side's air leaves through an exhaust port, and the rod is out. In the squeeze test below it, at 12 bar absolute, the air fills 150 cm³ and its rod is pushed in. The oil's rod has not moved.

pages.name: Where does the air go?
pages.task: Where does the air from the rod side go?
pages.answer: Out of an exhaust port, into the room
pages.why: The box -Y3 brings in joins the rod side to an exhaust port. So the used air leaves into the room. Oil is kept and used again, so the press sends it back to the tank.

pages.name: Pressure stays
pages.text: Stop stops the pump and switches both solenoids off. The springs centre the valve while the ram still presses the work. That shuts its oil in. The oil still holds the ram down, so its line turns red. Pressure shut in like this is stored energy. Now the pump has stopped, both solenoids are off and the gauge reads zero. The line from A is red, labelled still under pressure. The ram is still on the work.

pages.name: Safe to open?
pages.task: You must change the hose to the piston side. The motor is stopped and the pump's gauge reads zero. Is the hose safe to open?
pages.answer: No, oil shut in by the centred valve can still be under pressure
pages.why: The middle box blocks A. So the oil between A and the cylinder is shut in, and it still holds the ram on the work. Release that pressure and prove that part at zero before you open the hose.

pages.name: Top of the stroke
pages.task: -Y2 is still on and the ram has reached the top. Where does the pump's oil go now?
pages.answer: Over the relief valve to the tank
pages.why: At the end of its travel, no more oil can enter the rod side. The pressure climbs until the relief valve opens. Then the pump's oil goes over it to the tank. Switch -Y2 off and the P to T centre unloads the pump.
